paragraphs.text: Now after these things the Lord appointed seventy others, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself was about to come.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ κύριος καὶ ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα δύο καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: Meta de tauta anedeixen ho kyrios kai heterous hebdomēkonta dyo kai apesteilen autous ana dyo dyo pro prosōpou autou eis pasan polin kai topon hou ēmellen autos erchesthai.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, The harvest indeed is plenteous, but the laborers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he send forth laborers into his harvest.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι· δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐργάτας ἐκβάλῃ εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: elegen de pros autous· Ho men therismos polys, hoi de ergatai oligoi· deēthēte oun tou kyriou tou therismou hopōs ergatas ekbalē eis ton therismon autou.

paragraphs.text: Go your ways; behold, I send you forth as lambs in the midst of wolves.
paragraphs.original: ὑπάγετε· ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς ἄρνας ἐν μέσῳ λύκων.
paragraphs.translit: hypagete· idou apostellō hymas hōs arnas en mesō lykōn.

paragraphs.text: Carry no purse, no wallet, no shoes; and salute no man on the way.
paragraphs.original: μὴ βαστάζετε βαλλάντιον, μὴ πήραν, μὴ ὑποδήματα, καὶ μηδένα κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἀσπάσησθε.
paragraphs.translit: mē bastazete ballantion, mē pēran, mē hypodēmata, kai mēdena kata tēn hodon aspasēsthe.

paragraphs.text: And into whatsoever house ye shall enter, first say, Peace [be] to this house.
paragraphs.original: εἰς ἣν δʼ ἂν εἰσέλθητε οἰκίαν πρῶτον λέγετε· Εἰρήνη τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: eis hēn dʼ an eiselthēte oikian prōton legete· Eirēnē tō oikō toutō.

paragraphs.text: And if a son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon him: but if not, it shall turn to you again.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν ᾖ ἐκεῖ υἱὸς εἰρήνης, ἐπαναπαήσεται ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἀνακάμψει.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean ē ekei hyios eirēnēs, epanapaēsetai epʼ auton hē eirēnē hymōn· ei de mēge, ephʼ hymas anakampsei.

paragraphs.text: And in that same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the laborer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.
paragraphs.original: ἐν αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένετε, ἐσθίοντες καὶ πίνοντες τὰ παρʼ αὐτῶν, ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ. μὴ μεταβαίνετε ἐξ οἰκίας εἰς οἰκίαν.
paragraphs.translit: en autē de tē oikia menete, esthiontes kai pinontes ta parʼ autōn, axios gar ho ergatēs tou misthou autou. mē metabainete ex oikias eis oikian.

paragraphs.text: And into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you:
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν πόλιν εἰσέρχησθε καὶ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐσθίετε τὰ παρατιθέμενα ὑμῖν,
paragraphs.translit: kai eis hēn an polin eiserchēsthe kai dechōntai hymas, esthiete ta paratithemena hymin,

paragraphs.text: and heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.
paragraphs.original: καὶ θεραπεύετε τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ ἀσθενεῖς, καὶ λέγετε αὐτοῖς· Ἤγγικεν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai therapeuete tous en autē astheneis, kai legete autois· Ēngiken ephʼ hymas hē basileia tou theou.

paragraphs.text: But into whatsoever city ye shall enter, and they receive you not, go out into the streets thereof and say,
paragraphs.original: εἰς ἣν δʼ ἂν πόλιν εἰσέλθητε καὶ μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξελθόντες εἰς τὰς πλατείας αὐτῆς εἴπατε·
paragraphs.translit: eis hēn dʼ an polin eiselthēte kai mē dechōntai hymas, exelthontes eis tas plateias autēs eipate·

paragraphs.text: Even the dust from your city, that cleaveth to our feet, we wipe off against you: nevertheless know this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ τὸν κονιορτὸν τὸν κολληθέντα ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ὑμῶν εἰς τοὺς πόδας ἀπομασσόμεθα ὑμῖν· πλὴν τοῦτο γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ton koniorton ton kollēthenta hēmin ek tēs poleōs hymōn eis tous podas apomassometha hymin· plēn touto ginōskete hoti ēngiken hē basileia tou theou.

paragraphs.text: I say unto you, it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.
paragraphs.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι Σοδόμοις ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.
paragraphs.translit: legō hymin hoti Sodomois en tē hēmera ekeinē anektoteron estai ē tē polei ekeinē.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which were done in you, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
paragraphs.original: Οὐαί σοι, Χοραζίν· οὐαί σοι, Βηθσαϊδά· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν, πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ καθήμενοι μετενόησαν.
paragraphs.translit: Ouai soi, Chorazin· ouai soi, Bēthsaida· hoti ei en Tyrō kai Sidōni egenēthēsan hai dynameis hai genomenai en hymin, palai an en sakkō kai spodō kathēmenoi metenoēsan.

paragraphs.text: But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment, than for you.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν τῇ κρίσει ἢ ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: plēn Tyrō kai Sidōni anektoteron estai en tē krisei ē hymin.

paragraphs.text: And thou, Capernaum, shalt thou be exalted unto heaven? thou shalt be brought down unto Hades.
paragraphs.original: καὶ σύ, Καφαρναούμ, μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ; ἕως τοῦ ᾅδου καταβιβασθήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai sy, Kapharnaoum, mē heōs ouranou hypsōthēsē; heōs tou hadou katabibasthēsē.

paragraphs.text: He that heareth you heareth me; and he that rejecteth you rejecteth me; and he that rejecteth me rejecteth him that sent me.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ ἀκούων ὑμῶν ἐμοῦ ἀκούει, καὶ ὁ ἀθετῶν ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ ἀθετεῖ· ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ ἀθετῶν ἀθετεῖ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
paragraphs.translit: Ho akouōn hymōn emou akouei, kai ho athetōn hymas eme athetei· ho de eme athetōn athetei ton aposteilanta me.

paragraphs.text: And the seventy returned with joy, saying, Lord, even the demons are subject unto us in thy name.
paragraphs.original: Ὑπέστρεψαν δὲ οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα δύο μετὰ χαρᾶς λέγοντες· Κύριε, καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου.
paragraphs.translit: Hypestrepsan de hoi hebdomēkonta dyo meta charas legontes· Kyrie, kai ta daimonia hypotassetai hēmin en tō onomati sou.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, I beheld Satan fallen as lightning from heaven.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἐθεώρουν τὸν Σατανᾶν ὡς ἀστραπὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεσόντα.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de autois· Etheōroun ton Satanan hōs astrapēn ek tou ouranou pesonta.

paragraphs.text: Behold, I have given you authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall in any wise hurt you.
paragraphs.original: ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πατεῖν ἐπάνω ὄφεων καὶ σκορπίων, καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ, καὶ οὐδὲν ὑμᾶς οὐ μὴ ἀδικήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: idou dedōka hymin tēn exousian tou patein epanō opheōn kai skorpiōn, kai epi pasan tēn dynamin tou echthrou, kai ouden hymas ou mē adikēsē.

paragraphs.text: Nevertheless in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν ἐν τούτῳ μὴ χαίρετε ὅτι τὰ πνεύματα ὑμῖν ὑποτάσσεται, χαίρετε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν ἐγγέγραπται ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: plēn en toutō mē chairete hoti ta pneumata hymin hypotassetai, chairete de hoti ta onomata hymōn engegraptai en tois ouranois.

paragraphs.text: In that same hour he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou didst hide these things from the wise and understanding, and didst reveal them unto babes: yea, Father; for so it was well-pleasing in thy sight.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἠγαλλιάσατο τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι, πάτερ κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἀπέκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν, καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις· ναί, ὁ πατήρ, ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου.
paragraphs.translit: En autē tē hōra ēgalliasato tō pneumati tō hagiō kai eipen· Exomologoumai soi, pater kyrie tou ouranou kai tēs gēs, hoti apekrypsas tauta apo sophōn kai synetōn, kai apekalypsas auta nēpiois· nai, ho patēr, hoti houtōs eudokia egeneto emprosthen sou.

paragraphs.text: All things have been delivered unto me of my Father: and no one knoweth who the Son is, save the Father; and who the Father is, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son willeth to reveal [him].
paragraphs.original: πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ οὐδεὶς γινώσκει τίς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ, καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ πατὴρ εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι.
paragraphs.translit: panta moi paredothē hypo tou patros mou, kai oudeis ginōskei tis estin ho hyios ei mē ho patēr, kai tis estin ho patēr ei mē ho hyios kai hō ean boulētai ho hyios apokalypsai.

paragraphs.text: And turning to the disciples, he said privately, Blessed [are] the eyes which see the things that ye see:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς κατʼ ἰδίαν εἶπεν· Μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ οἱ βλέποντες ἃ βλέπετε.
paragraphs.translit: Kai strapheis pros tous mathētas katʼ idian eipen· Makarioi hoi ophthalmoi hoi blepontes ha blepete.

paragraphs.text: for I say unto you, that many prophets and kings desired to see the things which ye see, and saw them not; and to hear the things which ye hear, and heard them not.
paragraphs.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ βασιλεῖς ἠθέλησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ ὑμεῖς βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.
paragraphs.translit: legō gar hymin hoti polloi prophētai kai basileis ēthelēsan idein ha hymeis blepete kai ouk eidan, kai akousai ha akouete kai ouk ēkousan.

paragraphs.text: And behold, a certain lawyer stood up and made trial of him, saying, Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ νομικός τις ἀνέστη ἐκπειράζων αὐτὸν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;
paragraphs.translit: Kai idou nomikos tis anestē ekpeirazōn auton legōn· Didaskale, ti poiēsas zōēn aiōnion klēronomēsō;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τί γέγραπται; πῶς ἀναγινώσκεις;
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen pros auton· En tō nomō ti gegraptai; pōs anaginōskeis;

paragraphs.text: And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbor as thyself.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου, καὶ τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Agapēseis kyrion ton theon sou ex holēs tēs kardias sou kai en holē tē psychē sou kai en holē tē ischyi sou kai en holē tē dianoia sou, kai ton plēsion sou hōs seauton.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἀπεκρίθης· τοῦτο ποίει καὶ ζήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de autō· Orthōs apekrithēs· touto poiei kai zēsē.

paragraphs.text: But he, desiring to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbor?
paragraphs.original: Ὁ δὲ θέλων δικαιῶσαι ἑαυτὸν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Καὶ τίς ἐστίν μου πλησίον;
paragraphs.translit: Ho de thelōn dikaiōsai heauton eipen pros ton Iēsoun· Kai tis estin mou plēsion;

paragraphs.text: Jesus made answer and said, A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho; and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
paragraphs.original: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἄνθρωπός τις κατέβαινεν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Ἰεριχὼ καὶ λῃσταῖς περιέπεσεν, οἳ καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν καὶ πληγὰς ἐπιθέντες ἀπῆλθον ἀφέντες ἡμιθανῆ.
paragraphs.translit: hypolabōn de ho Iēsous eipen· Anthrōpos tis katebainen apo Ierousalēm eis Ierichō kai lēstais periepesen, hoi kai ekdysantes auton kai plēgas epithentes apēlthon aphentes hēmithanē.

paragraphs.text: And by chance a certain priest was going down that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
paragraphs.original: κατὰ συγκυρίαν δὲ ἱερεύς τις κατέβαινεν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν·
paragraphs.translit: kata synkyrian de hiereus tis katebainen en tē hodō ekeinē, kai idōn auton antiparēlthen·

paragraphs.text: And in like manner a Levite also, when he came to the place, and saw him, passed by on the other side.
paragraphs.original: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Λευίτης κατὰ τὸν τόπον ἐλθὼν καὶ ἰδὼν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν.
paragraphs.translit: homoiōs de kai Leuitēs kata ton topon elthōn kai idōn antiparēlthen.

paragraphs.text: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he was moved with compassion,
paragraphs.original: Σαμαρίτης δέ τις ὁδεύων ἦλθεν κατʼ αὐτὸν καὶ ἰδὼν ἐσπλαγχνίσθη,
paragraphs.translit: Samaritēs de tis hodeuōn ēlthen katʼ auton kai idōn esplanchnisthē,

paragraphs.text: and came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on [them] oil and wine; and he set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσελθὼν κατέδησεν τὰ τραύματα αὐτοῦ ἐπιχέων ἔλαιον καὶ οἶνον, ἐπιβιβάσας δὲ αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον κτῆνος ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν εἰς πανδοχεῖον καὶ ἐπεμελήθη αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai proselthōn katedēsen ta traumata autou epicheōn elaion kai oinon, epibibasas de auton epi to idion ktēnos ēgagen auton eis pandocheion kai epemelēthē autou.

paragraphs.text: And on the morrow he took out two shillings, and gave them to the host, and said, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, I, when I come back again, will repay thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον ἐκβαλὼν δύο δηνάρια ἔδωκεν τῷ πανδοχεῖ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐπιμελήθητι αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὅ τι ἂν προσδαπανήσῃς ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ ἐπανέρχεσθαί με ἀποδώσω σοι.
paragraphs.translit: kai epi tēn aurion ekbalōn dyo dēnaria edōken tō pandochei kai eipen· Epimelēthēti autou, kai ho ti an prosdapanēsēs egō en tō epanerchesthai me apodōsō soi.

paragraphs.text: Which of these three, thinkest thou, proved neighbor unto him that fell among the robbers?
paragraphs.original: τίς τούτων τῶν τριῶν πλησίον δοκεῖ σοι γεγονέναι τοῦ ἐμπεσόντος εἰς τοὺς λῃστάς;
paragraphs.translit: tis toutōn tōn triōn plēsion dokei soi gegonenai tou empesontos eis tous lēstas;

paragraphs.text: And he said, He that showed mercy on him. And Jesus said unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔλεος μετʼ αὐτοῦ. εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πορεύου καὶ σὺ ποίει ὁμοίως.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Ho poiēsas to eleos metʼ autou. eipen de autō ho Iēsous· Poreuou kai sy poiei homoiōs.

paragraphs.text: Now as they went on their way, he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι αὐτοὺς αὐτὸς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς κώμην τινά· γυνὴ δέ τις ὀνόματι Μάρθα ὑπεδέξατο αὐτὸν.
paragraphs.translit: En de tō poreuesthai autous autos eisēlthen eis kōmēn tina· gynē de tis onomati Martha hypedexato auton.

paragraphs.text: And she had a sister called Mary, who also sat at the Lord`s feet, and heard his word.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τῇδε ἦν ἀδελφὴ καλουμένη Μαριάμ, ἣ καὶ παρακαθεσθεῖσα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἤκουεν τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai tēde ēn adelphē kaloumenē Mariam, hē kai parakathestheisa pros tous podas tou Iēsou ēkouen ton logon autou.

paragraphs.text: But Martha was cumbered about much serving; and she came up to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister did leave me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ Μάρθα περιεσπᾶτο περὶ πολλὴν διακονίαν· ἐπιστᾶσα δὲ εἶπεν· Κύριε, οὐ μέλει σοι ὅτι ἡ ἀδελφή μου μόνην με κατέλειπεν διακονεῖν; εἰπὲ οὖν αὐτῇ ἵνα μοι συναντιλάβηται.
paragraphs.translit: hē de Martha periespato peri pollēn diakonian· epistasa de eipen· Kyrie, ou melei soi hoti hē adelphē mou monēn me kateleipen diakonein; eipe oun autē hina moi synantilabētai.

paragraphs.text: But the Lord answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art anxious and troubled about many things:
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ κύριος· Μάρθα Μάρθα, μεριμνᾷς καὶ θορυβάζῃ περὶ πολλά,
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de eipen autē ho kyrios· Martha Martha, merimnas kai thorybazē peri polla,

paragraphs.text: but one thing is needful: for Mary hath chosen the good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
paragraphs.original: ὀλίγων δέ ἐστιν χρεία ἢ ἑνός· Μαριὰμ γὰρ τὴν ἀγαθὴν μερίδα ἐξελέξατο ἥτις οὐκ ἀφαιρεθήσεται αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: oligōn de estin chreia ē henos· Mariam gar tēn agathēn merida exelexato hētis ouk aphairethēsetai autēs.
